data.headline: Regional banks' bad loans spark concerns on Wall Street
data.summary: Wall Street is concerned about the health of the nation’s regional banks, after a few of them wrote off bad loans to commercial customers in the last two weeks and caused investors to wonder if there might be more bad news to come.  Zions Bank, Western Alliance Bank and the investment bank Jefferies surprised investors by disclosing various bad investments on their books, sending their stocks falling sharply this week.  JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon added to the unease when he warned there might be more problems to come for banks with potentially bad loans.

data.headline: Capital One sues FDIC for overcharge related to two bank failures
data.summary: (Reuters) -Capital One sued the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, accusing the U.S. regulator of imposing an excessive $474.1 million special assessment to recoup losses to its deposit insurance fund following the collapses of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank in 2023.  The sixth-largest U.S. commercial bank said the FDIC "persists in seeking to collect a special assessment based on its erroneous calculation," despite two years of communications showing its math is wrong.
